working_title: The State Gave Them Sixty Minutes to Leave. Then It Said No One Was Ordered Out.
one_line: On 12 February 2017 Denise Johnson was walking into a supermarket in Oroville when strangers began shouting that everyone had to evacuate; five years later the state's answer to her claim for the two days it cost her was that no court could determine who had been ordered to leave, because no evacuation order had ever named a place.
contradiction: An American ordered out of her home by her own government would expect the order to be real enough to prove afterwards; instead, when Denise Johnson and 188,000 neighbours asked the state to repay the two days it cost them, the state's own evidence and the courts held that there was no defined mandatory evacuation zone and no defined group who had been ordered to go, and the people who left were ordered to pay the state's costs.

contradiction_form.normal_expectation: If the government orders you out of your house, there is an order, it covers somewhere, and you can show you were inside it.
contradiction_form.actual_outcome: The orders named 'the low levels of Oroville and areas downstream', 'the valley floor' and 'other communities along the Feather River'; the trial court found there was no means to determine whether any person fell inside a mandatory zone; class certification was denied and affirmed; DWR recovered its costs on appeal.
contradiction_form.gap: 188,000 people obeyed an order that, legally, was never issued to anybody in particular.

series_note: S15 AFTER THE DISASTER -- 'not the disaster, the system that starts the day after it ends' -- is the exact shape of this film. Alternates considered and rejected: S02 THIS SHOULDN'T BE POSSIBLE (fits the contradiction but sells the ruling, not the woman), S41 ONE DOCUMENT (the 12-page opinion could carry it, but the opening beat is a supermarket, not a filing), S17 THE SYSTEM FAILED (would make the dam the protagonist, which is what v001 got wrong).

runtime.basis: The documented spine is six primary-source moves (2005 FERC motion -> 12 Feb 2017 orders -> claims rejected autumn 2017 -> IFT report 5 Jan 2018 -> class denied 15 Mar 2022 -> DWR not a 'person' 5 Oct 2023) with four to five human fragments laid over it, none longer than a few hundred words. Forty-five minutes of that record is padding, and padding is banned. The 45-minute slot went to a different subject; do not re-open either decision here.

spine.name: Denise Johnson
spine.who: a renter in Oroville, Butte County; one of four named class representatives
spine.why_the_spine: Hers is the only sworn, first-person, named account of 12 February 2017 in hand, and the litigation follows her for five years, so the arc is continuous and carried by one face. She does not own the house she is told to leave, which is the channel's ordinary day exactly.
spine.sworn_account: In her declaration in support of the motion for class certification she stated that on 12 February 2017 she was walking into a supermarket when she heard people yelling that everyone had to evacuate because of an issue with the Oroville Dam's spillway; the supermarket then announced it was closing because of a mandatory evacuation and advised customers to go home and evacuate.

second_voice.name: Francis Bechtel
second_voice.who: a homeowner and resident of Butte County; the lead plaintiff
second_voice.sworn_account: He declared that he saw a mandatory evacuation order on the bottom of his television screen at approximately 3:00 p.m., and that about 15 minutes later a Butte County Sheriff's vehicle drove down his street and announced that residents had to leave their homes.
second_voice.why_he_matters: 3:00 p.m. is a full hour before the county's first order at 4:10 p.m. The television crawl reached him before the order existed. That single time-stamp is the film's first unexpected turn.

aftermath.name: Nicoli Nicholas
aftermath.who: operates a cattle ranch in Sutter County (complaint para. 44)
aftermath.documented_loss: Forced to evacuate hundreds of cattle, tons of baled hay and ranch equipment; relocation and return costs of at least $150,000. Some of his cows were infected with a virus -- possibly a species of Bovine Coronavirus, unknown on the Home Ranch -- while on the rangeland pastures they were moved to after the evacuation. After the return, calves born to those cows became infected and, despite intensive treatment, died. As of 27 January 2018, 81 of his calves had died.
aftermath.why_the_aftermath: It is the one consequence in the whole record that outlived the two days, and it is the film's proof that 'everyone went home' is not the same as 'nothing was lost'. It is the mid-point escalation and the last human beat before the courts take over -- never the spine, because a rancher sits one step outside the channel's ordinary-suburban register.

texture_only.name: Kaysi and Greg Levias
texture_only.use: the traffic, the boot, two boys and a dog, three weeks into a new Yuba City apartment. One snapshot, no follow-up exists. Opening-sequence second voice only.

justification.personal_relevance: 12 of 15, which is the 16-of-20 estimate in the protagonist search carried onto this scale unchanged, and deliberately not rounded up. The daily contact point is the house and the phone, and the system is a local government's emergency order -- something most Americans meet a handful of times in a life, not daily like a bank or a car. What lifts it well above v001's 12-of-20 is that the threat is no longer 'you might live below a dam' but 'a government can order you out of your home and then be unable to say whom it ordered', which is portable to every wildfire, hurricane, flood and chemical-spill evacuation any viewer has lived through. What holds it at 12 is that the contact is episodic.
justification.wtf_factor: 13 of 15. Two separate 'wait, that is allowed?' moments, both on the record and both verbatim: the trial court's finding that there was no defined mandatory evacuation zone and no defined group to which a mandatory order was issued, after 188,000 people left; and the disposition line ordering the evacuees to pay the state's costs on appeal. Short of 15 only because the reveal is a civil-procedure ruling, which takes forty seconds of setup before it detonates, where a 15 detonates on the sentence.
justification.human_stakes: 10 of 15, and this is the axis the film must not inflate. The realised loss to the protagonist is two nights out of a rented home and out-of-pocket expenses -- the plaintiffs pleaded exactly that and nothing more. Nobody died, nobody was hurt, everyone returned within two days. The larger documented losses belong to people who are not the spine: at least $150,000 and 81 dead calves (Nicholas), six rental homes at an estimated $50,000 each (Morton), a week's closure at about $10,000 (Parks). An 18-of-20 on this axis belongs to a seized life savings or eleven years in a cell; scoring this at that level would require leaning on the flood that did not happen, which is a counterfactual and is exactly the padding the owner banned.
justification.contradiction: 13 of 15, the rubric's primary feature and the reason this premise survives at all. It is a hard logical contradiction, not a grievance: ordered out, yet legally nobody was ordered; obeyed a mandatory order, yet no mandatory zone existed; asked for two days' expenses, and paid the state's costs instead. It is sourced to the court's own words rather than to a reporter's paraphrase. Short of 15 because it needs one clause of explanation ('class certification') that 'never charged, and the money is gone' does not.
justification.story_arc: 9 of 10, and only because the film commits to one named woman end to end. Seven beats, one face, every step on a document: she walks into a supermarket (sworn) -> strangers shout and the shop closes and tells her to leave (sworn) -> 4:10 p.m., then 4:34 p.m. and failure anticipated within 60 minutes (DWR's own evidence, verbatim) -> why nobody told her: the 17 October 2005 FERC motion and an unarmored hillside -> she joins 188,000 people asking for the cost of two days (her own complaint) -> the state's expert testifies that no one can determine who evacuated, the court finds there was no defined zone, the class dies, DWR recovers its costs -> and in 2023 the agency is held not to be a 'person' who can be fined at all. Not 10: the record of her life ends where the litigation ends, and we never learn what those two days actually cost her, which a 10 would require. This score is void if the film narrates 'residents' and cuts between six people instead; a composite drops it to 7.
justification.title_power: 8 of 10. Subject + Verb + Consequence lands cleanly and the strongest candidates carry a real number that no competing video has used: 'The State Gave Them Sixty Minutes to Leave. Then It Said No One Was Ordered Out.' Sixty minutes is what the county actually broadcast at 4:34 p.m.; the 'two hours' in the v001 working title is unsupported by this record and is retired here. Short of 10 because the payoff clause needs the word 'ordered' twice to make the contradiction legible, and the cleanest 10s do it with one verb.
justification.thumbnail_power: 7 of 10. Three separable single-subject images exist -- a woman frozen in a supermarket aisle, the 4:34 p.m. text with 'within the next 60 minutes' legible, and a county map with no zone drawn on it. The evidence variant is genuinely strong and fits the v002 shift away from movie-poster faces. Short of 10 because the single most striking image in the topic, the eroding hillside beside the intact concrete spillway, belongs to the film v001 wanted and not to this one: it sells the dam, and this film is not about the dam.
justification.evidence: 9 of 10. A 12-page appellate opinion quoting the sworn declarations and the trial court verbatim; four named class representatives with their own consolidated complaint; a 151-page complaint carrying the ranch losses and the rejected claims with dates; the county's four evacuation broadcasts timed to the minute from DWR's own opposition evidence; the 2005 FERC motion; the Independent Forensic Team report; the 2023 opinion. All public, all retrievable, all quotable on screen. Not 10 because the single most cinematic document -- the 90-page trial-court class-certification ruling -- is not in hand, and the government claim forms are scanned at an OCR quality this machine cannot read.
justification.broad_audience: 8 of 10. It reaches well beyond people interested in dams or in California, because the entrance is an evacuation order and roughly nobody in the American audience has never been told to leave somewhere or watched a neighbour be told. The measured base -- 77% aged 55+, 92.5% male -- is the demographic most likely to have lived through an evacuation and to own the house they were told to leave. Not 10 because there is no seized money, no cell door and no charge, and those are the three entrances this channel's audience is measured to click.
justification.franchiseability: 3 of 5. 'The order that was never an order' extends honestly to wildfire evacuation zones, hurricane orders, boil-water notices and shelter-in-place directives, and ten such films are plausible. A hundred is not, and the register measurement recorded below is the reason to be cautious: each one needs its own archive register, and this one came back amber, not the green that v001 assumed.
justification.evergreen: 4 of 5. The event is 2017 and the ruling is 2022, so nothing here expires; the mechanism -- an emergency order broad enough to move a city and too vague to prove afterwards -- is permanent and gets more relevant with every fire season. Short of 5 because the film is anchored to one dated crisis rather than to a rule a viewer meets on any ordinary Tuesday.

bonus_reasoning.specific_money_amount: AWARDED. Precise figures exist in primary filings and can be put on screen: at least $150,000 in relocation and return costs and 81 dead calves as of 27 January 2018 (SRC-0003, paras. 369-371); six rental homes at an estimated $50,000 each, claim filed 9 August 2017 and rejected 5 September 2017 (SRC-0003, paras. 263-265); about $10,000 for a few days' closure (SRC-0007).
bonus_reasoning.real_footage: NOT AWARDED, and this is the one that matters. Genuine 2017 spillway and evacuation footage plainly exists -- state agency video, network news, aerial coverage -- but the bonus requires it to be available AND CLEARABLE, and no clearance position on any specific clip has been established. Awarding it unverified would move the total from 85 to 90 and flip RESERVE to PRODUCTION, which is exactly why it is not awarded on an assumption. Establishing the rights position on California DWR's own published spillway footage is the single highest-value next check on this premise.
bonus_reasoning.recognizable_institution: NOT AWARDED. The honest reading of 'a name the audience already knows' is a brand or institution the viewer already carries into the click -- the v002 examples are corporate. 'Oroville Dam' was national news for a week in February 2017 and the California Department of Water Resources is not a household name nine years later. Awarding this would also flip the band, and a bonus that decides a band must not be awarded on a stretch.
bonus_reasoning.major_reversal: NOT AWARDED. The outcome never flips. Class certification was denied at trial and affirmed on appeal; the 2023 holding that DWR is not a 'person' is a different case with a different plaintiff and is not a reversal of anything in this one.

producibility.measured_by: claude, direct measurement over the shelf ledgers via scripts/shelf.py shelf_rows()
producibility.method: Video items only (31,150 on the shelf). Matched twelve sub-registers on WORD BOUNDARIES against title + matched_keywords + filename. Same-title re-ingests from one source collapsed to one item. Removed quarantined items, talking-head titles and anything the resolution index puts below 720p.
method_corrections: Substring matching was tried first and is wrong: 'rain' matches 'train', so 'subway train movement at night' entered the weather register.

The ledger `theme` field was tried and had to be dropped entirely. It is mislabelled at scale: 1,020 shelf videos carry theme `courtroom_justice`, among them 'walking to the mountain top'. Including it inflated the government/paperwork sub-register from 103 to 1,050. This is the documented factory-shelf mislabel trap and it is the mechanism by which a register can be reported abundant and turn out empty.
producibility.clips_available_labelled_note: distinct, HD or better, not talking-head, not quarantined. This is the figure comparable to how earlier registers were counted.

precision_sample.method: union-level random sample, seed 2017, judged by title against the question 'could this be placed in a 2017 Northern California small-town evacuation film without looking wrong?'. Foreign megacity traffic, satellite tornado imagery, money-rain effects, ocean storms and 3D city renders were judged off-register.

producibility.gate_reading: Amber on both denominators: 20.1% against the labelled register, 40.2% against the eyeball-corrected one, where the v002 thresholds are green <= 0.15, amber <= 0.40, red > 0.40. Dressable only with a staging plan named up front, which is what this section is.
producibility.v001_claim_not_reproduced: The v001 record claims 8,289 register clips and 4.8% utilisation at 45 minutes. No counting method reproduces 8,289 and none is recorded anywhere in the repository. Measured alternatives over the same shelf, using a deliberately over-broad 33-term net: video with strict word-boundary matching 3,182; video including the mislabelled theme field 5,247; video with loose substring matching 6,371; all media kinds strict 13,557. The nearest, 6,371, is 23% away and is reachable only by turning on both of the errors listed above. The 4.8% green in v001 should be treated as withdrawn, not as a second opinion.
thin_registers_named_up_front: EMERGENCY SHELTER: 1 clip on the whole shelf. Red Cross cots, fairground halls, families sleeping on a gym floor -- effectively zero inventory. The Silver Dollar Fairgrounds sequence cannot be dressed from the shelf and must be budgeted as stills, archive acquisition or a named reconstruction before the shot list is written.

DAM AND SPILLWAY: 29 clips, of which roughly half are genuine dams and none is Oroville. Sufficient for two or three cutaways and not for a sequence -- which suits this film, because it is not about the dam.
FLOOD AND EROSION: 22 clips. Enough for the 2005 warning beat, not enough for a flood act.
SUPERMARKET: 29 clips, several of them foreign shops. This carries the film's OPENING BEAT, so it is the register to verify by eye before anything else is commissioned.

CALIFORNIA PLACE: 44 clips, essentially all coastal, Los Angeles or Monterey. Northern California and Butte County inventory is zero. Establishing shots of the valley floor must come from stills or acquisition.
CATTLE: 72 clips, but the sample is dominated by sheep. Cows and calves specifically are a fraction of that, and the 81-calves beat needs them.

WHAT IS ABUNDANT: night traffic (538) and rain (307). Those two carry 65% of the register, which is why the gate is amber rather than green -- the film can always show cars and weather, and the beats that make it this film are the thin ones.
staging_plan_required_before_greenlight: Eyeball a labelled contact sheet of the supermarket, shelter, spillway and cattle sub-registers before any shot list is written. Filenames and relevance scores cannot tell an on-topic clip from an off-topic one; a human verdict can.
Budget the shelter sequence as a non-archive solution at the premise stage, not at assembly.

Do not solve thinness by generating more AI plates: solve_totals splits video proportionally to pool capacity, so a bigger AI pool pushes archive cuts off screen. The channel's normal shape is ~68% archive and 0% AI motion.
Footage diversity still binds: distinct >= 0.40, reuse <= 4, generic symbols <= 2. A register that is 65% traffic and rain is exactly the condition under which the same clip appears five times.

opening_beat.rule: It opens on the evacuation order reaching an ordinary person. Never on the document. Never on the water. Never on the sheriff's conference room. Person, then the abnormal event, then why, then the system -- in that order.
opening_beat.beat: A supermarket in Oroville, Sunday afternoon, 12 February 2017. A woman is walking in. She is not a homeowner, she is not a plaintiff, she is not anybody yet -- she is a person going into a shop. Then strangers start shouting.

first_sixty_seconds:
0:00. A supermarket entrance, from inside, looking out. Ordinary Sunday light. A woman walks in with the doors sliding shut behind her. No music yet, just the room tone of a shop. Narration, quiet and factual: 'On the afternoon of Sunday the twelfth of February, 2017, a woman named Denise Johnson walked into a supermarket in Oroville, California. She rented a house about a mile away. She was not expecting anything to happen.'

0:12. The sound of the shop changes -- voices, raised, overlapping, coming from somewhere off frame. We do not see the source. 'Somewhere behind her, people started shouting that everyone had to leave.' The shop's own announcement follows, and the film states plainly where this comes from: 'This is her account, given later under oath. The supermarket announced it was closing. Because of a mandatory evacuation. And it told its customers to go home and evacuate.' On screen, small and unglamorous, the citation: Declaration of Denise Johnson, quoted at page 6, Oroville Dam Cases, No. C090941.

0:26. Cut wide and cold: the town, emptying. Cars on a two-lane road with the light going. 'Within a few hours, one hundred and eighty-eight thousand people were told to leave their homes. Oroville. Marysville. Yuba City. The whole valley floor.'

0:34. The moment of truth device, early and deliberately: motion stops, music stops, one piece of text on a black frame, and the narrator reads it exactly as the county broadcast it at 4:34 that afternoon -- 'Officials now anticipate a failure of the Auxiliary Spillway at Oroville Dam within the next sixty minutes.' Hold on 'sixty minutes' for a full beat of silence.

0:44. Release. The film does not go to the dam. It goes forward five years, and states the thing the viewer cannot yet believe: 'Denise Johnson left. So did everyone she knew. And when she later asked the State of California to pay back what those two days had cost her, the state's answer -- and then the court's -- was that nobody could determine who had been ordered to leave.'

0:56. The question that runs the film, spoken once and never repeated: 'Because the order had never named anywhere in particular.' Title card. Then the second voice -- Francis Bechtel, who saw it on his television at three o'clock, an hour before the county issued anything at all.

retired.title: They Warned the Government in 2005. In 2017, 188,000 People Had Two Hours to Leave.
retired.why: 'Two hours' is not supported by the record. The figure the county actually broadcast at 4:34 p.m. was failure anticipated 'within the next 60 minutes'. Sixty minutes is both accurate and stronger, and must replace it everywhere.

hard_constraints.rule: Oroville Dam Cases, No. C090941 (Cal. Ct. App. 3d, filed 3/15/22) is NOT TO BE PUBLISHED. It must never be described as precedent, as settled law, as 'the courts have ruled', or as binding on anyone but these four people. Its own first page records that California Rules of Court, rule 8.1115(a) prohibits courts and parties from citing or relying on opinions not certified for publication. That restricts lawyers in California courts and does not restrict journalism -- but calling it precedent on screen would simply be false.

Francis Bechtel, Jacob Klein, Chantel Ramirez, Denise Johnson, Marie Giordano and Carol A. Gissell are private individuals who sued and lost. They were accused of nothing. They must be presented as people a system failed to accommodate -- they asked for two days' expenses and were told the order that emptied their town was too vague to prove they had been told to leave. Never as failed litigants, never as opportunistic, never with a line that invites the viewer to think they overreached.

The JCCP 4974 pleadings name individual DWR employees in connection with allegations of racist conduct and theft. No court has ever found any of it true; a motion to strike was denied only on the technicality that an identical unchallenged complaint carried the same words. Those employee names must not appear anywhere -- not in the script, not in research notes that feed the script, not in on-screen documents, not in the description. Likewise the former DWR employee whose harassment suit and settlement appear as exhibits to the Harriman declaration: a private individual, a victim, and irrelevant to the evacuation.

Every narrated factual sentence carries a source id from the `sources` block below. A sentence with no source id does not enter the script. This is the standing rule and it is repeated here because this topic's record contains four attractive facts that are NOT verified and are listed in `not_verified`.

The protagonist is Denise Johnson and the film says so. It must not narrate 'residents' and cut between six people. If it becomes a composite, story_arc is 7, not 9, and this score is void. Where a second person's account is used, the film states on screen that it is a different person.

No AI-generated image or motion may be presented as an authentic record of the 2017 crisis, and no real person's likeness may be generated. Reconstructions are labelled on screen and disclosed. This includes the supermarket in the opening beat.

Say sixty minutes, not two hours. The county's 4:34 p.m. broadcast anticipated failure 'within the next 60 minutes'. The 'two hours' figure carried in earlier planning notes is unsupported and is retired.

quotes.text: In fact, the evidence and briefing submitted to the trial court demonstrated there was no defined mandatory evacuation zone and no defined group to which a mandatory evacuation order was issued.

they did not describe a specific area but rather such vague areas as: 'low levels of Oroville and areas downstream,' the portion of Yuba County that is 'on the valley floor,' and 'other communities along [the] Feather River.'
This lack of ascertainability would also prevent individual class members from self-identifying as meeting the class definition.

There is simply no means by which to readily determine whether a residence or person falls within a 'mandatory' evacuation zone, whether the resident actually evacuated, and which order (if any) caused that person to evacuate.
Dr. Cova stated there is no known method to enumerate who evacuated and who did not in a given area and time frame in response to a broadcasted evacuation order.
The judgment is affirmed. Respondent Department of Water Resources shall recover its costs on appeal.

the_court_in_its_own_words.closing_beat: The people who were ordered out of their homes were ordered to pay the state's costs of proving they could not be identified as having been ordered out of their homes.

risk.ban_risk: LOW. Zero deaths, the defendant is a state agency, and no living private individual is accused of anything. The rights and fairness exposure is entirely in HC-2 and HC-3 -- naming the wrong people, or framing the six plaintiffs as losers.
risk.litigation_status: Closed. C090941 affirmed 15 March 2022; C093600 decided 5 October 2023. Nothing here is live, so the 'do not conclude while litigation is live' rule does not bind -- but HC-1 still does.
